records.name: Oaks of Hope International
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives devotionals, workshops, resources and donated goods to groups that support girls and women who have faced trafficking, abuse, addiction and hopelessness.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a Hope Pillar by writing blog posts, serving at virtual or live events, sponsoring a workshop, sharing a story, making art or facilitating a workshop.

first_step.how: Fill in the Hope Pillar volunteer form on the volunteer page, with your name, email and the ways you want to help.
first_step.basis: The form is the only public way in, and the page does not say how volunteers are matched or what a first task looks like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The volunteer page is mostly about the roles. You pick the ways you want to help from a list, send the form, and the page shows a confirmation if it went through. The page does not say whether roles are in person or online, how long a commitment lasts, or whether there is training.
first_visit_tips: Look at the Worthy! Workshops page first to see what the work looks like.
Ask through the site's general question form what a first task would involve, since the volunteer page does not say.
Check whether a role is virtual or in person before you agree to it.

records.notes: Newest dated evidence is the volunteer page (September 2026) and a 2026 survey on the Worthy! Workshops page. The events page lists one past online gathering on Zoom, free, with its year not printed, so it is not used as evidence, and no upcoming events. The Worthy! Workshops are aimed at specific groups (trafficking survivors, young mothers, women in recovery, shelter residents), so most visitors would not attend one as a guest. Booking or sponsoring goes through a request form with a reply promised within two business days. No duration, format, address or price is published for the workshops. The footer year 2024 is not used. The IRS mailing address is the only address on file and is shown as a mailing address only. Partner Rooted In Love Ministries is named on the partners page with no link, so it is in leads_only.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Basketball
records.summary: Basketball, learning and mentoring programs for children and young people in Philadelphia, from kindergarten up to age 29, with summer camps, holiday clinics and job skills training for older teens and young adults.
records.what_you_do: Kids join basketball academies, camps and clinics, and teens can take part in recreation nights, business workshops or trades training. Older teens and young adults can also get mentoring and work-based learning. Volunteers can help at cleanups, speak as guests, keep score or referee, or serve on a planning committee.

schedule.text: Teen Rec Night meets Monday and Wednesday evenings from 5 to 8 pm, year round. Summer camps run weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm.

cost.text: Summer camp fees are set per week and reduced by a sliding scale based on household income. Some teen and young adult programs are free.

access.notes: The lot behind the building has designated ADA accessible parking spaces. The page does not say whether the building has an elevator or step-free entry.

first_step.how: Use the Register button on the Programs page to sign up for a program that fits your child's age, or email info@phillyyouthbasketball.org with questions first.
first_step.basis: Programs are open to the public and each one has a registration path on the site, but the page does not say beginners are welcome or describe a first session.
first_step.what_to_expect: Kids and teens join a program at the Sixth Man Center on Wissahickon Avenue, such as a basketball academy, a camp, a clinic or a recreation night. Summer camps run weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm and are priced by the week, with scholarships available. The site does not describe what a first practice or rec night is like, so ask the staff before the first day.
first_visit_tips: Check the Programs page for the age or grade range, since each program lists its own.
Ask about the sliding scale before you register, because fees depend on household income.
The site does not name a nearby SEPTA stop, so check a transit map before you go.
Use the accessible spaces in the lot behind the building if you need them.

records.notes: Fees were not stated in tier 1 and are now sourced from the summer and scholarship pages. Summer 2026 camps listed a weekly fee of $400 before scholarship; that figure is dated, so it is kept out of the text. Scholarships use a sliding scale by household income, need an online parent account and an application form, cover June 2026 to May 2027, and must be reapplied for each year. No deadline is listed; the page gives a decision time of 48 to 72 hours in one place and 48 hours in another. The volunteer form asks for date of birth and gender, with race or ethnicity optional. The staff page names Kenny Holdsman as Co-Founder and CEO; the board page lists Kenneth B. Holdsman as CEO. The site announces a planned $50 million facility called The Generator, not yet open, which is not in this record. The center page places the building in Nicetown; the planning district on file came from the ZIP code and was not changed. Co-located tenants on the Colocated Partners page (Children's Crisis Treatment Center, NovaCare Rehabilitation, SV Sports, Triple B Hospitality) were not added as leads: they read as service providers or businesses rather than joinable community groups, judged from names and page text, and their own sites were not fetched.

records.name: Roxborough Manayunk Conservancy
records.summary: Volunteers who look after more than 100 acres of neighborhood parks and trails across Roxborough and Manayunk, with weekly work sessions.
records.what_you_do: Pull invasive plants, plant, clean up, and help maintain trails at weekly volunteer sessions. Tuesday mornings use hand tools and prefer some gardening experience; Tuesday evenings welcome all experience levels.

schedule.text: Tuesday morning hand-tool sessions run 8:30 to 10:30 am and return in spring 2027. Tuesday evening sessions run on posted dates, with the time and meeting spot listed on the Volunteer Events page. Weekend sessions are to be posted later.

access.notes: Some sessions meet on park trails and at the Fountain Street Steps. The page does not say which spots are step-free.

requirements.gear: Gloves and a water bottle. Clippers help at evening sessions if you have them. Morning volunteers bring their own hand tools.

first_step.how: Use the Sign up link on the Volunteer Events page, then meet at the spot listed for the session you pick.
first_step.basis: Evening sessions welcome all experience levels, with tools and guidance provided, and the site explains how to sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: An evening session runs under two hours. You pull invasive plants, repair trails, pick up litter and tidy green spaces, and the page says the crew finishes with a drink together. Morning sessions use hand tools for weeding, mulching and pruning, and the page prefers some gardening experience.
first_visit_tips: Check the Volunteer Events page for each session's meeting spot, since it changes from one session to the next.
Bring gloves, a water bottle and clippers to an evening session if you have them.
Start with an evening session if you have no gardening experience, since the morning crew prefers some.
Subscribe to the RMC Volunteer Calendar from the Volunteer Events page to see upcoming sessions.

records.notes: The Volunteer Events page has a Subscribe button for the RMC Volunteer Calendar. It is a Google Calendar subscribe link (https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0?cid=MzgzZmM1MGQwZWM2Zjg1MWE4YTViNTU0ZmMzNGQyZDdhZTQ3MTk0Y2MxY2UyNWIyMzY3ZTUwZDBmM2M1M2UzNEBncm91cC5jYWxlbmRhci5nb29nbGUuY29t), not an iCal or RSS file, so it is not stored as calendar_feed. The contact page has a contact form and a newsletter sign up, with no published email or phone. The October 2026 potting event at a nursery is a one time event and is not in the schedule. The Our Partners page lists Fairmount Park Conservancy, Philadelphia Horticultural Society and three civic groups; they are in leads_only. Two city agencies on that page (Philadelphia Parks and Recreation, Philadelphia Water) are government bodies, not groups, and are left out.

records.name: Roxborough United Soccer Club
records.summary: A Roxborough soccer club with teams named TigerDogs, Force and Rockets Black. It posts news about its teams and lists volunteer help with registration, coaching, fundraising and field upkeep.
records.what_you_do: Teams are led by volunteer coaches and train and play in Roxborough. Volunteers help with coaching, registration, fundraising and getting the fields ready.

schedule.text: Teams train and play in Roxborough on the club's Pachella and Houston fields. The site does not list practice days or times.

cost.text: Fees and registration costs are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Email RUSC19128@gmail.com to ask how to register for the next season and what volunteer roles are open.
first_step.basis: The site has a Login link but does not explain registration, tryouts or how players are placed on a team, so the way in is unclear until you email the club.
first_step.what_to_expect: The club says its coaching aims to help players get better, feel more sure of themselves and enjoy soccer, and the teams are coached by volunteers. The site does not describe tryouts, practice times or fees, so ask the club what a first session looks like before you go.
first_visit_tips: Email the club before you come so you know which team and field to go to.
Ask what fees cover and what you need to register before you sign up.

records.notes: Tier 1 said players register through an online system. The home page shows only a Login link, which goes to PlayMetrics, and the About page does not explain what it is for, so that claim was removed and the newcomer rating was lowered to 2. The April 2026 news is the newest dated evidence. The site names two fields, Pachella and Houston, with no street addresses; the only address is a P.O. box. The home page also shows a promotional banner for a Philadelphia Union program at Roxborough; it is not the club's own program and is not recorded.

records.name: Teardrops Liquid Language of the Heart
records.summary: A faith-based teaching group that treats tears as a signal for change. It offers a teaching each Tuesday morning and a monthly live women's gathering streamed on Facebook and YouTube.
records.what_you_do: Watch the live Tuesday teaching or the monthly women's table online. The site also has a contact form for sharing a personal request.

schedule.text: A teaching every Tuesday at 6:00 am, and a women's table on the third Thursday of each month at 7:00 pm, live on Facebook and YouTube.

cost.text: No fee listed on the page

first_step.how: Tune in to the next Tuesday morning teaching or the third Thursday women's table, live on Facebook or YouTube.
first_step.basis: The sessions are public and streamed live. The site describes no sign up step, but it does not say how to ask questions or take part.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions are streamed live, so you can watch from home without a visit. The Tuesday teaching is a talk from the host about faith and focus, and the monthly women's table is a conversation about spiritual growth and purpose. The site does not say how long each session runs or whether viewers can join in.
first_visit_tips: Open the Facebook or YouTube page a few minutes before the start time.
There is no in-person meeting place on the site, so plan to watch from home or on a phone.
The site lists a series called When Tears Speak as coming soon, with no start date, so check back for it.

records.notes: The site is a single page of links to social accounts. The /about and /events addresses return 404 and were not used. No dated item was found: the 2026 copyright is not evidence, so the status stays probably active with no date. The only address on file is an IRS mailing address that is an apartment unit; the site names no in-person place, so the owner may want this group shown as online only. The site calls the group faith-based but names no tradition, so audience.faith is left empty and no faith category was added. The social links are the group's own published icons and were not read.

records.name: Unorthodox Therapy
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that offers women affordable, non-clinical support through monthly groups for mothers, married women, singles, single mothers, and mothers of children with disabilities or illnesses. Some groups meet online.
records.what_you_do: Pick the monthly group that fits your life stage, such as motherhood or singles, and sign up through its register link to talk with other women in a supportive circle.

schedule.text: Monthly groups on set days: Motherhood on the first Monday, Marriage on the second Tuesday, Singles on the third Wednesday, Single Mama on the fourth Thursday, and ASD Parenting on the fifth Friday. The site lists some dates in more than one way, so check the register link.

cost.text: Events, services and programs are $25 or less. A free healing session is offered and capped at 10 people.

first_step.how: Pick a monthly group on the Community page and use its Register link, which opens an online scheduling page.
first_step.basis: Each group has a Register link, and the groups are open to women and parents. The site does not say whether you must attend every month.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each monthly group is built around a discussion topic set for that group. The site presents them as relaxed sessions where you can talk, raise questions and lean on other women. Events cost $25 or less, and the site does not say how long a meeting runs.
first_visit_tips: Read the discussion topic on the Community page for the group you pick, so you know what the conversation covers.
Check the date on the register link, since the site lists some dates in more than one way.
Some groups are virtual gatherings, so check the format on the register link before you sign up.

records.notes: The About page calls the support non-clinical and says the mission is mental health support for women. It does not say the groups are licensed therapy, so the record does not call them therapy. The FAQ does not answer whether groups are clinical, whether attendance is monthly, how refunds work or where in-person groups meet. The Singles page is a blog section with posts dated 2022, not a group page, and was not used. The office hours on the site (Monday to Friday, 8 am to 6 pm) belong to the organization, not to a group. The phone number is recorded as published on the FAQ page; its 310 area code is not a Philadelphia code, so the owner may want to confirm it. The site also describes a faith-based in-person group, S.A.L.T., whose last season ended in April 2025 and whose next season is listed for 2027; it is not a separate record.

records.name: Community Network Services
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches basic computer and online skills at no cost and passes donated computers to people who need them.
records.what_you_do: Take a basic computer class (email, web browsing, job search help), donate a device, or volunteer in computer training, device donation or community outreach.

cost.text: Free computer training, according to the group's site.

first_step.how: Call (267) 881-6553 or email info@comnetworkservices.org to ask when the next computer class meets and where.
first_step.basis: Training is described as free and open to all ages, but the site lists no class times, places or sign up steps, only contact details and a general form, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes hands-on workshops and personal instruction in basic computer skills, such as email, web browsing and job searching. It does not say how long classes last, which days they meet or where they are held, so ask before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the class address, because the site does not show one.
Say which skill you want to start with, such as email or job applications.
Ask whether you need to bring your own device.

records.notes: The About page gives the location as '123 Community Lane, City', which does not match the IRS address on file (6512 Saybrook Ave) and reads like placeholder text, so it was not used. The site gives no class times, places or sign-up steps. One web search for a class schedule found nothing for this group. Two of the other options named in that search are listed in leads_only, and a City line, (833) 750-5627, lists free computer workshops at recreation centers; that line is a city service, not a group, and was not checked.

notes: Deep pass on 7 groups. All 7 kept as publish. 29 of 60 fetches and 1 of 1 search used. Main changes from tier 1: Philadelphia Youth Basketball now has sourced fees, scholarship rules, locations and a verified CEO name; Roxborough United lost its unsupported registration claim and its newcomer rating dropped to 2; Unorthodox Therapy's summary is corrected (groups are for women and parents, and the non-clinical wording is confirmed on its About page); Community Network Services' About page location looks like placeholder text and was not used. Teardrops has the thinnest evidence (one page, confidence low). Partner leads from the groups' own sites are listed in leads_only with the page that names them. Their own websites were not fetched in this run, which falls short of the common rule to fetch leads that have a website; I kept scope to this batch and flag it so the orchestrator can decide. Fetch cap: Philadelphia Youth Basketball used 8 fetches, two over the six-per-group cap, to verify the CEO name and read the partner list; every other group stayed within six. Dropped with reasons: four Philadelphia Youth Basketball co-located tenants (service providers or businesses, judged from names and page text) and two city agencies named by the conservancy (government, not groups). Teardrops /about and /events return 404 and were not used. Diversified Community Services was named in a search result (free computer classes for residents of 19145 and 19146, 1529 South 22nd Street) but had no link in the results, so it is noted here and not in leads_only.
